objective: Test whether distilled TRIAXIS/EBRC mechanisms add decision-quality lift beyond simpler matched-call/output-budget baselines on an actually weak external model without teaching the target abstention mechanism in the shared contract.

predecessor_experiment.reason: H00 and the shared v0.1 contract explicitly instructed the model not to invent missing information/quantities, creating CONTRACT_TEACHES_MECHANISM risk for the main answerability discriminator.

frozen_external_subject: same 20 UMWP cases and same private oracle as v0.1
model_rail: OpenRouter free route only; do not substitute paid model or Hugging Face Job

interpretation.expand_condition: At least one non-H00 arm produces a concrete task-level rescue pattern not offset by harms and not attributable to parsing/schema differences.
interpretation.collapse_condition: If H00 matches the richer arms on all 20 cases, or simpler H09 matches H13/H14 with lower or equal protocol complexity, do not credit integrated TRIAXIS lift from this benchmark.

budget_matching.reason: Protocol prompts differ in input length; v0.2 matches call count and output ceiling and reports provider token usage. This is a screening comparison, not a confirmatory equal-compute estimate.

residual_design_risks: The shared schema permits answer=null, so the model can infer that a non-numeric outcome is representationally possible. The contract does not state when to use null or mention missing information/answerability; therefore this is mechanism-hidden, not latent-task-unaware.
UMWP20 exposes no external tool/verifier. H14 therefore tests compact-state/commitment orchestration only, not the full WMX externalized-verifier capability.
Different arm prompts have different input-token lengths; provider token usage must be reported and no confirmatory equal-compute claim is allowed.
